svg.title: Grounded intelligence on AWS — relay mode and hosted-index mode

g.text: Grounded intelligence on AWS — relay mode and hosted-index mode
Relay (default cloud mode): the desktop retrieves locally and sends only consented context. Hosted index: opt-in folders indexed in Aurora (private subnets, no NAT, VPC endpoints).
1 · Relay mode: the desktop retrieves locally (FTS5 + vectors + graph), filters by scope, redacts, and sends question + context.
2 · The relay receives the request with the user's JWT.
3 · It checks the vault's consent mode, the model allowlist and the remaining token budget (atomic counter).
4 · Guardrails screen the assembled context for prompt attacks and sensitive data before any model call.
5 · The model (chosen by family, with a fallback order) answers, citing only the chunk ids it was given.
6 · The answer streams back; the desktop's verifier resolves each citation to revision + span and flags unsupported claims.
7 · Hosted index (opt-in): only consented folders are uploaded, encrypted with the tenant's KMS key. Excluded paths never leave.
8 · Each object event is queued, with retries and a dead-letter queue.
9 · The indexer chunks by heading (about 350–650 tokens) with stable anchors: document + section + span + hash.
10 · Embeddings come from Bedrock over a VPC endpoint; model id and version are recorded (a new model = a new namespace).
11 · Chunks, tsvector, vectors and link edges are upserted in one transaction; obsolete chunks are removed.
12 · Web companion: the user asks a question through the same API and JWT.
13 · In hosted mode the relay asks the retriever instead of receiving context from a device.
14 · Lexical, vector and graph channels run separately under row-level security, then fuse with RRF and an optional rerank; then steps 4–5 run.
15 · Revoking consent deletes the objects and propagates to chunks, vectors and summaries.
